mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 4%, it predicts a forward discounting effect that boosts S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day pre-trigger average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) above 150,000 suggests labor market strength, which correlates with higher corporate earnings expectations and positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns under strong employment are not significantly above the 30-day pre-trigger mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105 indicates weakening supply-side demand, which tends to precede negative S&P 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day pre-signal average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in housing starts (HOUST) by over 10% signal supply-side contraction, which amplifies equity valuation sensitivity and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly < previous * 0.90 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns do not deviate from baseline by at least 1% (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 2-month moving average of UNRATE falls below 3.5%, the forward discount rate is expected to rise, reducing expected equity valuations and producing negative S&P 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly lower than the 30-day pre-trigger mean (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in consumer spending (CPIAUCSL) above 284.5 suggests demand resilience, which is associated with positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day pre-trigger average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in both industrial production (INDPRO) and consumer spending (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% in the same month indicate dual softening, which amplifies negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not significantly worse than the average of the two univariate signals (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a prolonged period of falling inflation (CPIAUCSL < 273 for 3 consecutive months), S&P 20-day forward returns tend to be positive due to reduced discounting pressure.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not positive in at least 70% of such regimes (empirical frequency test).
